haiku-low.q3: A 5-minute timer calls secrets.refresh(). A changed value replaces the in-memory one and logs the version id. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries at the next tick.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first (secrets.load() at pod start); /healthz returns 200 (ready) only after all three keys have loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The pod never becomes ready, so the rollout stops/halts. Old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A refresh timer every 5 minutes calls secrets.refresh() to re-read the three secrets; a changed value replaces the in-memory value and the new version id is logged. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries at the next tick; pods keep serving.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory. They must never go on disk, into environment variables, or into logs.
sonnet.q5: Only the security on-call writes prod secrets. Prod read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Engineers cannot read prod values.
sonnet.q6: Because git history keeps the keys (history is not rewritten) and earlier images still contain them, so the keys are treated as leaked. Rotation at the providers with revocation of the old keys last makes the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: The clients (payments, email, geocoding) call secrets.get(name) on every provider call and do not copy the key when built, so the refreshed in-memory key is used immediately.
sonnet.q8: After refresh (within 5 minutes), each pod logs the new version id, and the team confirms all 4 pods show the new version id in /healthz secret_versions. Only then revoke the old key; if any pod doesn't show it, do not revoke.
sonnet.q9: 1) Access policies; 2) create secrets (copy current keys into store); 3-7) app code switching to store, clients, /healthz, removing keys from config file, local runs, shipped as one release; 8) deploy and verify; 9) rotate keys at providers and revoke old ones last; 10) update rollback notes.
sonnet.q10: From the dev secrets orders-api/dev/* in the store (sandbox keys), via make run with APP_ENV=dev, using engineers' own read access to dev secrets only. No prod secret is needed.
sonnet.q11: A missing prod secret makes it fail at start the same as an unreachable store: the process exits non-zero (after retries), the pod never becomes ready, the rollout stops, and old pods keep serving. The document does not say specifically about partial loading beyond this.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided on a rotation schedule; no cadence is chosen.
